sentences.text: The holotype specimen, PMO 216.839, is a partially preserved juvenile plesiosaur.
The genus was named after Øystein Djupedal, a former Norwegian minister who funded the excavation with 1.2 million kroner.
Fossils were discovered in 2009 in Spitsbergen within the Agardhfjellet Formation.
Djupedalia belongs to the family Cryptoclididae.
The fossils are dated to the middle Volgian stage, and the animal lived in the uppermost Jurassic in central Spitsbergen, Norway.
The genus lived between 149.2 and 143.1 million years ago during the Tithonian stage.
